questions.q: Extreme chilliness, so that the patient wants the head covered even in summer, with offensive discharges and despair of recovery, calls for:
questions.why: Psorinum is very chilly, wants warm clothing in summer, has filthy-smelling discharges and despairs of recovery. Sulphur is a hot patient.

questions.q: After digestion, long-chain fatty acids leave the intestinal cells mainly as:
opts: fatty acids bound to albumin in the hepatic artery
free fatty acids entering the portal vein
questions.why: Long-chain fats are re-esterified and packed into chylomicrons, which enter the lymph via lacteals; short-chain fatty acids go to the portal blood.

questions.q: Allergic rhinitis with violent sneezing, and itching of the palate, worse from the smell of flowers, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Sabadilla: hay fever.

questions.q: A great desire for fresh air, burning pains relieved by heat, and offensive, foul-smelling discharges with a history of never being well since a suppressed eruption suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Psorinum: chilly, offensive, despair of recovery; 'never well since'.

questions.q: Rigor mortis first appears in the:
opts: Myocardium (and then the eyelids and face)
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Heart first, then eyelids, face, and downward (Nysten's rule).

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, a desire for salt is found in the chapter:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Food desires and aversions are rubrics under Stomach in Kent.

questions.q: Who proved Lachesis in 1828 and is called the father of American homoeopathy?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Hering also gave the law of direction of cure.

questions.q: According to §150, a patient complaining of one or a few trivial symptoms of recent origin, removable by a change of diet or regimen, has:
opts: an indisposition, not a real disease needing medicine
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §150: indispositions need only removal of the exciting cause.

questions.q: After about 24 hours of fasting, blood glucose is maintained mainly by:
opts: absorption of glucose from the gut
release of free glucose from muscle glycogen
questions.why: Liver glycogen is largely used up within about a day; muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase and cannot release free glucose.

questions.q: By Hahnemann's method, how long does the trituration of one centesimal potency take?
questions.why: Each potency takes one hour: three periods of 20 minutes, each of 6 minutes' grinding and 4 minutes' scraping, done twice.
